stem:
In parallelogram $PQRS$, $\angle P=70^\circ$.

Which claim about the angles is correct?

options.text: Adjacent $\angle Q=70^\circ+110^\circ=180^\circ$ as a single angle measure at $Q$.

teacher.key_rationale: In a parallelogram, adjacent angles sum to 180° and opposite angles are equal, so Q=110° and R=70°. Swapping those values reverses the adjacent/opposite rules. Not every angle is 70°. Adding 70 and 110 describes the supplementary pair, not the measure of one angle Q.
